rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 tier-1 toolbox] Gidney 2018 temporary AND: a Toffoli PAIR that computes and later uncomputes the same AND costs 4 T total - 4 T to compute, 0 T to uncompute via X-basis measurement + classically controlled CZ fix-up. Clean pairs (target declared zero-init, |0> before, unwritten between) take temporary_and directly on the target; any pair with unchanged controls takes it via a fresh ancilla (via_ancilla: true) with cx(ancilla, target) at both ends.
rules.note: (z = -0.71 at call 6)

rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 tier-1 toolbox] Jones Toffoli / measurement-based uncompute: ANY single ccx or ccz costs 4 T + 1 fresh clean ancilla + 1 measurement (jones_toffoli) - AND into the ancilla (4 T), cx/cz(ancilla, target), then measure the ancilla and fix up with Cliffords. Use it for unpaired Toffolis that have no clean target.
rules.note: (z = -0.60 at call 8)

rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 tier-1 toolbox] Clean-AND compute-only: a Toffoli whose target is a declared zero-init qubit still |0> at that point is a pure AND - 4 T, no measurement, no uncompute (clean_and). Typical for the first write into an output register (multiplier-like accumulation).
rules.note: (z = +0.72 at call 8)

rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 tier-1 toolbox] Relative-phase Toffoli pairing (Maslov RCCX): a mirror pair (same Toffoli repeated, target only READ in between) can use the 4-T relative-phase Toffoli on BOTH members - the second cancels the first's phase, so the pair is EXACT (8 T, unitary-preserving). Never use RCCX on a lone Toffoli: the uncancelled phase is an error.
rules.note: (z = +3.25 at call 2)

rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 tier-1 routing lesson] Mirror pair writing into a declared-zero target => temporary-AND: when the recognizer shows a pair whose target is a declared zero-init qubit (class 'clean'), temporary_and on the target is strictly cheaper than any exact route (4 T vs 8+ T) and the relaxed verifier certifies it branch-wise. Route clean pairs FIRST; they are the highest-value decisions on adder-like structure.
rules.note: (z = +0.81 at call 6)

rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 tier-1 toolbox] MCX cascades: an unpaired Toffoli whose controls are targets of enclosing pairs is a multi-controlled X built from an AND ladder. Relaxed: ancilla_mcx (every enclosing pair -> temporary_and, middle -> jones_toffoli, 4 T per element). Exact: barenco_mcx (pairs -> relative_phase_toffoli 8 T each, middle 7 T).
rules.note: (z = -1.03 at call 16)

rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 literature harvest] Whole-adder pairing strategy: in a Cuccaro-style ripple adder ALL BUT ONE Toffoli appears in a compute/uncompute pair. Plan the WHOLE circuit before deciding any element: classify every Toffoli into pairs first, route every pair as temporary_and (4 T), and only the leftover unpaired Toffoli(s) as jones_toffoli (4 T) - this is what turns 7n naive T into 4n+O(1), not per-element greediness.
rules.note: (z = -1.53 at call 15)

rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 literature harvest] Compute/uncompute asymmetry: computing a temporary AND costs 4 T but UNcomputing it costs 0 T (X-basis measurement + classically controlled CZ fixup - measurement is not reversible, use it). When a plan can choose which side of a pair carries the T cost, put it on the compute side; an out-of-place register that is later uncomputed is uncomputed for free under the relaxed contract.
rules.note: (z = +0.90 at call 17)

rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 literature harvest] Ancilla-vs-T tradeoff for multi-controlled gates: best known k-control X is 4k-4 T using k-1 CLEAN ancillas (temporary-AND ladder); Barenco-style constructions save ancillas at a LARGE T increase. Fitness is lexicographic with T first: whenever declared-zero ancillas exist, take ancilla_mcx; reserve barenco_mcx for genuinely qubit-starved circuits.
rules.note: (z = +1.64 at call 7)

rules.text: [seed 2026-10-18 literature harvest] Floor awareness: a measurement-FREE compute/uncompute Toffoli block costs >= 8 T (isotropy lower bound); only measurement-based routes reach 4 T per pair. A relaxed plan at 4 T per paired element and 4 per unpaired (jones), or an exact plan at 8 per pair and 7 per unpaired, sits AT the known floor - further T proposals are wasted calls; propose qubit or T-depth improvements instead, or decline (NONE).
rules.note: provenance: 'Exact T-counts of Toffoli layers from an isotropy bound', arXiv:2610.01024 (2026)

rules.text: Floor check BEFORE proposing: relaxed lower bound = 4 T per compute/uncompute PAIR (not per element, since the uncompute is free) + 4 T per unpaired Toffoli. Exact bound = 8 per pair + 7 per unpaired. If the parent's t_count already equals that bound, answer NONE. Re-submitting the same plan is rejected as 'no improvement'.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 18: Duplicate of R15. R15 adds the point that the floor is measured against the current parent. Keeping both wastes prompt space and shows the same floor check twic)

rules.text: Pre-submit count: list each Toffoli as pair-compute (4 T), pair-uncompute (0 T, measurement fix-up), or unpaired (4 T jones). Sum them and compare with the parent's t_count. Submit only if the sum is strictly lower. A plan that reproduces the parent's per-element routes gives 'no improvement' (e.g. 16 -> 16) and wastes the call.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 18: Duplicates R11's floor check and the 'no improvement' warning. Shown 2 times with no measured lift (0/2 improving prompts), so it only adds prompt length.)

rules.text: When the parent is already a relaxed plan at the floor, do not switch relaxed routes to exact ones (temporary_and/jones -> RCCX/Barenco). That raises T (4 -> 8 per pair) and is rejected. Exact routes are only for when the task demands unitary equality; otherwise leave the paired and unpaired routes unchanged and decline.

Decline check FIRST: if the parent's t_count equals the floor (relaxed: 4 per compute/uncompute pair + 4 per unpaired Toffoli; exact: 8 per pair + 7 per unpaired), reply NONE. In recent runs 8 of 10 metric rejections were the same plan resubmitted at 16 -> 16, and none of the 16 calls declined. Declining costs nothing; a resubmission is always rejected as 'no improvement'.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 9: Duplicates R11 and R13 (decline when the parent is at the floor). Its evidence is weak (shown 3, improving 0/3), and its claim that no call declined is now outd)

rules.text: Floor check BEFORE proposing, measured against the CURRENT parent, not the original baseline. Relaxed bound = 4 T per compute/uncompute pair + 4 per unpaired Toffoli. Exact bound = 8 per pair + 7 per unpaired. If the parent's t_count already equals the bound (or is below any plan you can build), answer NONE. A child that equals or exceeds the parent's t_count is rejected as 'no improvement'.

Plans must cover every occurrence: the accepted plan used x26 for each of T0..T15, while repeated plans with x10 per type were rejected as 'no improvement (112 -> 112)'. Copy the multiplicity of the CURRENT parent's plan and change routes, not counts. Never resubmit any plan string listed under recent rejections.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 18: Redundant with R18, which gives the same multiplicity-copying instruction with more accepted evidence. Keeping both spends prompt space on one lesson.)

rules.text: Floor check BEFORE proposing, against the CURRENT parent (after any accepted child), not the original baseline of 112. Relaxed bound = 4 T per compute/uncompute pair + 4 per unpaired Toffoli. Exact bound = 8 per pair + 7 per unpaired. If parent t_count already equals the bound (e.g. a relaxed plan at 32), answer NONE. A child with t_count >= parent's is rejected.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 9: Near-verbatim duplicate of R15 (same floor check against the current parent, same bounds, same NONE answer). Keeping both wastes prompt space.)

rules.text: Plan multiplicities must match the CURRENT parent's per-type occurrence counts (accepted: x13/x26 mix at 84->36, then x6 for all 12 types at 36->16). Never submit a uniform guess like x10 per type: it was rejected 5 times (36 -> 84). Copy the counts from the parent plan or recognizer output. If they are not visible, answer NONE rather than guess.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 9: Duplicate of R20. Its 12-type 84->36->16 history does not match the current 7-type 49->16 task, so it misleads the proposer about the baseline.)

rules.text: Re-read the parent's t_count before every proposal. Accepted children cut it 84 -> 36 -> 16, so the baseline in the task text is stale. A plan that changes no routes and only resubmits previously tried counts will score at or above the parent and be rejected as 'no improvement'. Propose only if you can name which type's route changes and why its per-element T drops; otherwise answer NONE.
rules.note: (z = -1.04 at call 19)

rules.text: Plan multiplicities must be copied from the CURRENT parent's plan or the recognizer's per-type counts. Accepted: x13/x26 mix (84->36), then x6 for all 12 types (36->16). Uniform guesses (x10 per type) were rejected 6 times as 'no improvement (84 -> 84)'. If the counts are not visible, answer NONE rather than guess. Change routes, never counts.

Output format: emit exactly one line plan[...] with entries 'T<k>x<N>' separated by ', ' and sorted as strings (T0, T1, T10, T11, T2, ..., T9), matching accepted plans. No prose, no code fences inside the plan, and no type names that are not in the parent's plan. Parse errors have cost calls; a malformed plan is lost even if its routes are right.

Plan multiplicities must come from the recognizer's per-type counts or the CURRENT parent plan, never a uniform guess. Observed: at t_count 49 with types T0..T6, plan[T0x13, T1x13, T2x13, T3x13, T4x13, T5x13, T6x13] was accepted (49->16) twice; x10 per type was rejected 5 times (49->49). If counts are not visible, answer NONE.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 18: Duplicates R20 (copy multiplicities from the parent plan or recognizer counts, never uniform guesses). It has 0/5 improving prompts and adds prompt length witho)

rules.text: Each type T<k> may be named by exactly ONE decision. A plan rejected with 'T0 is named by two decisions (M0 and P0)' tried to use T0 as both a paired temporary-AND (P) and an unpaired jones/MCX (M). Pick one route per type, based on whether the recognizer shows that type as a compute/uncompute pair or as unpaired.

Verbatim-resubmit check: if your plan string is identical to the parent's plan (e.g. plan[T0x13, T1x13, T2x13, T3x13, T4x13, T5x13, T6x13] when t_count is already 16), it is rejected as 'no improvement (16 -> 16)'. This happened 7 times. Compare your output to the parent plan before emitting; if they match, answer NONE.

Copy multiplicities from the CURRENT parent's plan or the recognizer's per-type counts. Uniform guesses (x10 per type) were rejected as 'no improvement (84 -> 84)'. Accepted plans changed routes, not the heavy counts. If counts are not visible, answer NONE rather than guess.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 18: Near-verbatim duplicate of R20 (copy multiplicities from the parent; uniform x10 guesses are rejected). It adds no new information and only dilutes the prompt.)

rules.text: Do not shrink the multiplicity of the heaviest types. Lowering T0 and T10 from x26 to x6 was rejected 5 times by the verifier ('wrong output: support [0x8] != [0xc]'). Keep T0x26 and T10x26 and keep T5x13. The accepted 24-T plan keeps those three and uses x6 on T1-T4 and T6-T9.

Before emitting a plan, check each type's count against the parent. If your T0, T5 and T10 counts differ from the accepted pattern (T0x26, T5x13, T10x26), assume the function changes and the verifier will reject it. If the parent already scores 24 and your plan can only match it, answer NONE.
rules.note: (retired by reflector at call 18: Redundant with R26 and R24. Its heavy-type pattern (T0x26, T5x13, T10x26) and its 'parent at 24, answer NONE' check are folded into the edited R26.)

rules.text: Heavy types are fixed: keep T0x26, T5x13, T10x26. Shrinking T0/T10 to x6 was rejected 5 times ('wrong output: support [0x8] != [0xc]'). The light types T1-T4 and T6-T9 are the only tunable ones. Evidence: x13 gave 77->40, x6 gave 77->24, and x26 only tied at 24->24. Once the parent is at 24, any light-type multiplicity change cannot lower T, so answer NONE.
